abstract: Despite the increasing deployment of virtual streamers in e-commerce livestreaming, their effectiveness remains inconsistent. Drawing on the concept of intelligent interactivity, the authors examine how and why responsiveness and response naturalness interactively shape downstream outcomes in virtual livestreaming. They further test when the presence of a livestream assistant can enhance the effect of responsiveness under low response naturalness. One recall study and five experiments show that virtual streamers’ high responsiveness results in a higher likelihood of purchase intention and livestreaming continuance when their response naturalness is high, but this effect is nonexistent when naturalness is low. Moreover, this interactive effect can be explained by dual social influence processes: internalization of mental imagery and consumer–virtual streamer identification. In addition, the effect of responsiveness on both purchase intention and livestreaming continuance via mental imagery quality is only evident when a human livestream assistant is present in the low-naturalness context. The findings contribute to the emerging field of virtual livestreaming and the design of digital human interactivity. The authors also offer practical insights to e-commerce marketers and virtual streamer developers seeking to improve the effectiveness of virtual livestreaming.

ur.tldr: 研究虚拟主播在电商直播中的有效性机制。通过回忆研究和多实验设计，考察响应性与回应自然性的交互效应，发现高响应性需配合高自然性才能提升购买意愿和直播继续意愿，否则无显著作用。心理意象质量和消费者-虚拟主播认同起中介作用，人类直播助手可弥补低自然性的不足，为虚拟主播设计优化提供理论依据。

title: EXPRESS: Toward Intelligent Virtual Streamers: Leveraging Responsiveness and Response Naturalness in E-commerce Livestreaming
title_zh: EXPRESS：迈向智能虚拟主播：利用响应能力与回应自然度提升电商直播
